dataset: Devign & Big-Vul Security Benchmark (augmented for multi-language AST transfer)
model_architecture: CodeBERT-base (12-layer, 768-hidden, 12-heads, 125M parameters) fine-tuned with binary classification head

per_vulnerability_type.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials / API Keys

limitations: The neural model was primarily pre-trained and fine-tuned on C/C++ security benchmarks. Inferences on JavaScript, TypeScript, and HTML rely on cross-language token embeddings and syntactic similarity, which are unvalidated on full web frameworks.
Dual-signal design: GenForge runs both the ML model and a deterministic AST/regex pattern scanner concurrently. Never treat either signal as an absolute certification of security.
False negatives can occur in complex distributed state, dynamic property resolution, or obfuscated payloads.
Pattern matching enforces hard rules (e.g. banning eval, innerHTML sinks, plain-text secret keys), while the model provides semantic vulnerability probability.
